title: Legislative districts of Lanao del Norte

{{Short description|Legislative districts of the Philippines}} {{Use dmy dates|date=July 2022}} {{Politics of the Philippines}} The '''legislative districts of Lanao del Norte''' are the representations of the [[Provinces of the Philippines|province]] of [[Lanao del Norte]] in the [[List of legislatures of the Philippines|various national legislatures]] of the [[Philippines]]. The province is currently represented in the [[House of Representatives of the Philippines|lower house]] of the [[Congress of the Philippines]] through its [[#1st District|first]] and [[#2nd District|second]] congressional districts. The [[Cities of the Philippines#Independent cities|highly urbanized city]] of [[Iligan]] last formed part of its representation in 2010. == History == {{further|Legislative district of Mindanao and Sulu|Legislative district of Lanao}} Prior to gaining separate representation, areas now under the jurisdiction of Lanao del Norte were represented under the [[Department of Mindanao and Sulu]] (1917–1935) and the historical [[Lanao (province)|Lanao Province]] (1935–1961).{{fact|date=November 2023}} The enactment of Republic Act No. 2228 on 22 May 1959 divided the old Lanao Province into [[Lanao del Norte]] and [[Lanao del Sur]], and provided them each with a congressional representative.{{cite web|author=Congress of the Philippines|title=Republic Act No. 2228 - An Act to Create the Provinces of Lanao del Norte and Lanao del Sur|url=http://laws.chanrobles.com/republicacts/22_republicacts.php?id=2231 |website=Chan Robles Virtual Law Library|access-date=18 February 2017|date=22 May 1959}} In accordance with Section 8 of R.A. 2228, the incumbent representative of Lanao Province, Laurentino Badelles, continued to represent both successor provinces until the [[1961 Philippine general election|next general election in 1961]]. The chartered city of [[Iligan]], despite being enumerated as part of the territory of neither successor province, was designated as Lanao del Norte's seat of provincial government and became part of [[#Lone District (defunct)|its congressional representation]].{{fact|date=November 2023}} Lanao del Norte was represented in the [[Interim Batasang Pambansa]] as part of [[Interim Batasang Pambansa#Regional Representatives|Region XII]] from 1978 to 1984. The province returned [[#At-Large (defunct)|one representative, elected at large]], to the [[Regular Batasang Pambansa]] in [[1984 Philippine parliamentary election|1984]]. [[Iligan]], declared a [[highly urbanized city]] in 1983, separately elected its [[Legislative district of Iligan#At-Large (defunct)|own representative]] in this election.{{fact|date=November 2023}} Under the new Constitution{{cite web|title=1987 Constitution of the Philippines - Apportionment Ordinance|url=http://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/constitutions/the-1987-constitution-of-the-republic-of-the-philippines/the-1987-constitution-of-the-republic-of-the-philippines-ordinance/|author=1986 Constitutional Commission|date=2 February 1987|access-date=19 November 2017|website=Official Gazette of the Republic of the Philippines}} which was proclaimed on 11 February 1987, Lanao del Norte was once more grouped with Iligan and reapportioned into two [[House of Representatives of the Philippines#District representation|congressional districts]], which elected their respective members to the restored House of Representatives starting [[1987 Philippine legislative election|that same year]].{{fact|date=November 2023}} The passage of Republic Act No. 9724 on 20 October 2009, segregated the [[highly urbanized city]] of [[Iligan]] from the [[#1987–2010|first district of Lanao del Norte]] to form its [[Legislative district of Iligan|own congressional district]] starting in the [[2010 Philippine general election|2010 elections]].{{cite web|url=http://www.senate.gov.ph/republic_acts/ra%209724.pdf|title=Republic Act No. 9724 - An Act Separating the City of Iligan from the First Legislative District of the Province of Lanao del Norte to Constitute the Lone Legislative District of the City of Iligan|author=Congress of the Philippines|date=20 October 2009|access-date=18 February 2017 |website=Senate of the Philippines}} Republic Act No. 9774, enacted on 17 November 2009, further reapportioned Lanao del Norte's districts by transferring the municipalities of [[Balo-i]], [[Matungao]], [[Pantar, Lanao del Norte|Pantar]] and [[Tagoloan, Lanao del Norte|Tagoloan]] from the [[#2nd District|second]] to the [[#1st District|first]] district.{{cite web|title=Republic Act No. 9774 - An Act providing for the reapportionment of legislative districts in the Province of Lanao del Norte|author=Congress of the Philippines|date=17 November 2009|access-date=18 February 2017|website=Senate of the Philippines|url=http://www.senate.gov.ph/republic_acts/ra%209774.pdf}} The reconfigured districts elected their representatives beginning in the [[2010 Philippine general election|2010 elections]]. == 1st District == *'''[[Municipalities of the Philippines|Municipalities]]''': [[Bacolod, Lanao del Norte|Bacolod]], [[Balo-i]], [[Baroy]], [[Kauswagan]], [[Kolambugan]], [[Linamon]], [[Maigo]], [[Matungao]], [[Pantar, Lanao del Norte|Pantar]], [[Tagoloan, Lanao del Norte|Tagoloan]], [[Tubod, Lanao del Norte|Tubod]] *'''Population (2015)''': 295,473{{cite web|url=https://psa.gov.ph/sites/default/files/attachments/hsd/pressrelease/2015_Table%201_Legislative%20Districts.xlsx|website=Philippine Statistics Authority|date=2015|title=Population of Population of Legislative Districts by Region, Province, and Selected Highly Urbanized/Component City: 2015|access-date=22 November 2017}} {| class="wikitable" style="text-align:center; width:40%;" |- ! width="40%"| Period !
